title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政 Volume 53 Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十三‧列傳第三十四 良政

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53 — Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 傅琰 虞愿 劉懷慰 裴昭明 沈憲 李珪之 孔琇之

translations.literal: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, Kong Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan; Yu Yuan; Liu Huaiwei; Pei Zhaoming; Shen Xian; Li Guizhi; Kong Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 太祖承宋氏奢縱，風移百城，輔立幼主，思振民瘼。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor inherited the Song dynasty's extravagance and indulgence; customs had shifted in a hundred cities. He assisted in establishing a young sovereign and sought to revive the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder Emperor took power after the Song dynasty's era of extravagance and excess, when customs had shifted across the realm. He helped install a young ruler and set out to relieve the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 爲政未朞，擢山陰令傅琰爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: His government had not yet reached its term when he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before his reign had run its course, he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 乃捐華反樸，恭己南面，導民以躬，意存勿擾。

translations.literal: He then cast off splendor and returned to simplicity, bowed to himself facing south, guided the people by his own example, and kept in mind not to disturb them.
translations.idiomatic: He then abandoned display for simplicity, governed with restrained dignity, led the people by personal example, and aimed at non-interference.

sentences.zh: 以山陰大邑，獄訟繁滋，建元三年，別置獄丞，與建康爲比。

translations.literal: Because Shanyin was a great district and lawsuits proliferated, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison aide was appointed, on a par with Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanyin was a major county with proliferating lawsuits, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison aide was appointed, matching the setup at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 永明繼運，垂心治術。

translations.literal: When the Yongming reign succeeded, he devoted his heart to the art of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongming reign that followed, the court devoted itself to the art of governance.

sentences.zh: 杖威善斷，猶多漏網，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。

translations.literal: He wielded authority and judged well, yet many still escaped the net; when senior officials violated the law, the blade was sealed and execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded authority and judged firmly, yet many still slipped through; when senior officials broke the law, execution followed without delay.

sentences.zh: 郡縣居職，以三周爲小滿。

translations.literal: For those holding office in commanderies and counties, three years was taken as a small fulfillment of tenure.
translations.idiomatic: Officials serving in commanderies and counties were expected to complete a three-year term as a basic tenure.

sentences.zh: 水旱之災，輙加賑卹。

translations.literal: When flood or drought disasters occurred, relief and succor were always added.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever floods or droughts struck, relief was promptly provided.

sentences.zh: 明帝自在布衣，曉達吏事，君臨億兆，專務刀筆，未嘗枉法申恩，守宰以之肅震。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, from the time he was a commoner, understood administrative affairs thoroughly. When he ruled over the myriad people, he devoted himself solely to documents and the brush; he never bent the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates were awed and shaken thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a commoner, Emperor Ming had mastered administrative affairs. Once he ruled the realm, he devoted himself to paperwork and legal procedure, never bending the law to show favor; prefects and magistrates were awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 永明之世，十許年中，百姓無雞鳴犬吠之警，都邑之盛，士女富逸，歌聲舞節，袨服華粧，桃花綠水之間，秋月春風之下，蓋以百數。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, for some ten years the common people had no alarm of crowing cocks or barking dogs. The capital's prosperity — men and women rich and at ease, songs and dance, splendid dress and fine adornment, between peach blossoms and green waters, under autumn moon and spring breeze — amounted to hundreds upon hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, for roughly ten years the people knew no disturbance. The capital flourished: men and women lived in comfort, with song, dance, fine dress, and ornament everywhere — between peach blossom and green water, under autumn moon and spring breeze — in hundreds upon hundreds of such scenes.

sentences.zh: 及建武之興，虜難猋急，征役連歲，不遑啓居，軍國糜耗，從此衰矣。

translations.literal: When the Jianwu reign arose, barbarian troubles surged urgently; conscription and corvée continued year after year; there was no leisure to open one's door; army and state were consumed and wasted — from this the decline began.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwu reign began, frontier crises intensified; conscription ran year after year without respite; army and state were drained — and decline set in from that point.

sentences.zh: 齊世善政著名表績無幾焉，位次遷升，非直止乎城邑。

translations.literal: In the Qi era, those famous for good government and manifest achievement were few; rank and promotion were not confined merely to cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi, officials famed for good government and visible achievement were few; promotions were not limited to urban posts alone.

sentences.zh: 今取其清察有迹者，餘則隨以附焉。

translations.literal: Now we take those whose clarity and scrutiny left traces; the rest are appended as they come.
translations.idiomatic: Here we select those whose clarity and diligence left a clear record; the remainder are included where relevant.

sentences.zh: 傅琰字季珪，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yan, styled Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was from Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邵，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was an Attendant Outside the Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao served as Attendant Outside the Office.

sentences.zh: 父僧祐，安東錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Sengyou was Recorder of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyou was Recorder under the Eastern Expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，遷山陰令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was transferred to magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 山陰，東土大縣，難爲長官，僧祐在縣有稱，琰尤明察，又著能名。

translations.literal: Shanyin was a great county of the eastern lands and hard to govern as chief official. Sengyou had a reputation in the county; Yan was especially keen in scrutiny and also gained a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin was a major eastern county and a difficult post. Sengyou had earned repute there; Yan was especially sharp in judgment and also became known for competence.

sentences.zh: 其年爵新亭侯。

translations.literal: That year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era he was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，居南岸，隣家失火，延燒琰屋，琰抱柩不動，隣人競來赴救，乃得俱全。

translations.literal: When his mother died he dwelt on the south bank. A neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to Yan's dwelling. Yan embraced the coffin and did not move; neighbors rushed to rescue him, and all were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he lived on the south bank. A neighbor's fire spread to his house; Yan held the coffin and would not move. Neighbors rushed to help, and both he and the coffin escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 琰股髀之閒，已被煙焰。

translations.literal: Between Yan's thighs and buttocks he had already been touched by smoke and flame.
translations.idiomatic: The skin between his thighs had already been scorched by smoke and flame.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除邵陵王左軍諮議，江夏王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultant of the Left Army under the Prince of Shaoling and Recorder under the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultant of the Left Army to the Prince of Shaoling and Recorder to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰爲山陰令。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor assisted in government, because lawsuits piled up in Shanyin, Yan was again made magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder Emperor held regency, lawsuits in Shanyin piled up, and Yan was again appointed magistrate there.

sentences.zh: 賣針賣糖老姥爭團絲，來詣琰，琰不辨覈，縳團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。

translations.literal: An old woman who sold needles and an old woman who sold sugar disputed over a ball of silk and came before Yan. Yan did not examine and verify; he bound the ball of silk to a pillar and flogged it, secretly observing that there were iron filings — then punished the sugar seller.
translations.idiomatic: An old needle-seller and an old sugar-seller disputed a ball of silk before Yan. Without questioning them, he tied the silk to a pillar and whipped it; watching closely, he saw iron filings — and fined the sugar-seller.

sentences.zh: 二野父爭雞，琰各問「何以食雞」，一人云「粟」，一人云「豆」，乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。

translations.literal: Two rustics disputed over a chicken. Yan asked each, "What do you feed the chicken?" One said "millet," one said "beans." He then broke open the chicken and found millet, and convicted the one who had said beans.
translations.idiomatic: Two farmers disputed a chicken. Yan asked each what he fed it — one said millet, one beans. He slaughtered the bird, found millet inside, and convicted the man who had said beans.

sentences.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢復爲偷盜。

translations.literal: Within the county he was called divine in insight; none dared steal again.
translations.idiomatic: The county hailed him as uncannily perceptive; no one dared steal again.

sentences.zh: 琰父子竝著奇績，江左鮮有。

translations.literal: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records, rarely seen in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary administrative records, rarely matched south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 世云「諸傅有《治縣譜》，子孫相傳，不以示人」。

translations.literal: The age says, "All the Fu clan have a Manual of Governing Counties, handed down from generation to generation and not shown to others."
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that the Fu clan possessed a Manual of Governing Counties, passed down through generations and never shown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 臨淮劉玄明亦有吏能，爲山陰令，大著名績。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had administrative ability; as magistrate of Shanyin he achieved great renown in achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had administrative talent; as magistrate of Shanyin he won great renown.

sentences.zh: 琰子翽問之，玄明曰：「我臨去當告卿。

translations.literal: Yan's son Ao asked him; Xuanming said, "When I am about to leave I shall tell you."
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Ao asked his secret; Xuanming said, "When I am leaving I will tell you."

sentences.zh: 」將別，謂之曰：「作縣唯日食一升飰，而莫飲酒。」

translations.literal: " As they were about to part he said to him, "In governing a county, eat only one sheng of rice a day and do not drink wine."
translations.idiomatic: At parting he said, "Governing a county: eat only one sheng of rice a day — and never drink wine."

sentences.zh: 虞愿字士恭，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan, styled Shigong, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan, courtesy name Shigong, was from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖賚，給事中，監利侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fen was a Supernumerary Attendant and Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fen was Supernumerary Attendant and Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 父望之，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wangzhi died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wangzhi died young.

sentences.zh: 賚中庭橘樹冬熟，子孫競來取之，愿年數歲，獨不取，賚及家人皆異之。

translations.literal: A tangerine tree in the courtyard of Fen ripened in winter; grandchildren competed to pick the fruit. Yuan, only a few years old, alone did not take any; Fen and the whole family all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: A courtyard tangerine ripened in winter at Fen's home; grandchildren rushed to pick the fruit. Yuan, only a few years old, alone refrained — to the astonishment of Fen and the household.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，爲國子生，再遷湘東王國常侍，轉潯陽王府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia he became a student of the Imperial University, was twice promoted to Attendant of Constant Service in the Kingdom of Xiangdong, and transferred to Ink-Copying Staff Officer in the mansion of the Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia he entered the Imperial University, rose twice to Attendant of Constant Service in the Kingdom of Xiangdong, then became Ink Office staff officer in the Prince of Xunyang's household.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，以愿儒吏學涉，兼蕃國舊恩，意遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, because Yuan was learned in both Confucian and administrative studies and also enjoyed old favor from the princely state, he was treated with exceptional regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yuan — versed in both scholarship and administration and favored from old ties to the princely household — received exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 除太常丞，尚書祠部郎，通直散騎侍郎，領五郡中正，祠部郎如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Imperial Secretariat, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and concurrently head of the Five-Commandery Selection Office, while retaining his post as Director of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of Rites in the Secretariat, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and head of the Five-Commandery Selection Office, while retaining his Rites post.

sentences.zh: 帝性猜忌，體肥憎風，夏月常著皮小衣，拜左右二人爲司風令史，風起方面，輙先啓聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor was suspicious by nature, corpulent and hating wind; in summer he often wore a small leather garment. He appointed two attendants at his side as Wind-Reporting Clerks; whenever wind rose from any quarter they would report first.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was suspicious by nature, stout and averse to wind; in summer he often wore a small leather jacket. He named two attendants Wind-Reporting Clerks who announced any breeze from any direction.

sentences.zh: 星文災變，不信太史，不聽外奏，勑靈臺知星二人給愿，常直內省，有異先啓，以相檢察。

translations.literal: For astral omens and calamitous changes he did not trust the Grand Astrologer and would not hear outside memorials; he ordered two star-knowers of the Observatory assigned to Yuan, constantly on duty in the inner palace; if anything was unusual they reported first for mutual inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He distrusted the Grand Astrologer on celestial omens and barred outside reports, assigning two Observatory star-knowers to Yuan on constant inner-palace duty to report anomalies for cross-checking.

sentences.zh: 帝以故宅起湘宮寺，費極奢侈。

translations.literal: The Emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence at extreme expense.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence at ruinous expense.

sentences.zh: 以孝武莊嚴剎七層，帝欲起十層，不可立，分爲兩剎，各五層。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories, the Emperor wished to build ten; it could not stand, so it was divided into two monasteries of five stories each.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories; the Emperor wanted ten but the structure would not bear it, so he built two five-story monasteries instead.

sentences.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡還，見帝，曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi, Grand Administrator of Xin'an, finished his term and returned; seeing the Emperor he said, "Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple yet?
translations.idiomatic: When Xin'an Grand Administrator Chao Shangzhi returned from his post and saw the Emperor, he asked, "Have you visited the Xiang Palace Temple yet?

sentences.zh: 我起此寺，是大功德。

translations.literal: I raised this temple — it is great merit.
translations.idiomatic: I built this temple — a great act of merit.

sentences.zh: 」愿在側曰：「陛下起此寺，皆是百姓賣兒貼婦錢，佛若有知，當悲哭哀愍，罪高佛圖，有何功德？

translations.literal: " Yuan at his side said, "Your Majesty raised this temple entirely with money from common people selling their sons and pawning their wives. If the Buddha had knowledge, he would weep in grief and pity; the sin towers above the Buddha-image — what merit is there?
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan beside him said, "Your Majesty built this temple with money from people who sold their children and pawned their wives. If the Buddha knew, he would weep; the sin exceeds any Buddha-image — what merit is there?

sentences.zh: 」尚書令袁粲在坐，爲之失色。

translations.literal: " Yuan Ji, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was present and turned pale at this.
translations.idiomatic: " Secretariat Director Yuan Ji, present, turned pale.

sentences.zh: 帝乃怒，使人驅下殿，愿徐去無異容。

translations.literal: The Emperor then grew angry and had someone drive him from the hall; Yuan departed slowly without change of expression.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew furious and had him driven from the hall; Yuan left slowly, unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩，少日中，已復召入。

translations.literal: Because of old favor, within half a day he was summoned back in.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to old favor, within half a day he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 帝好圍碁，甚拙，去格七八道，物議共欺爲第三品。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved weiqi but was very clumsy, leaving the grid by seven or eight lines; public opinion together deceived him into rating third class.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved weiqi but played poorly, often misplacing stones by seven or eight lines; court opinion humored him with a third-rank rating.

sentences.zh: 與第一品王抗圍碁，依品賭戲，抗每饒借之，曰：「皇帝飛碁，臣抗不能斷。

translations.literal: Playing weiqi with first-rank Wang Kang, wagering by rank, Kang always gave him advantages and said, "The Emperor's flying stones — your servant Kang cannot cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Against first-rank Wang Kang he wagered by rank; Kang always let him win, saying, "When Your Majesty's stones fly, this subject cannot block them.

sentences.zh: 」帝終不覺，以爲信然，好之愈篤。

translations.literal: " The Emperor never perceived it, believed it true, and loved the game all the more ardently.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor never caught on, took it for truth, and loved the game all the more.

sentences.zh: 愿又曰：「堯以此教丹朱，非人主所宜好也。

translations.literal: Yuan also said, "Yao used this to teach Danzhu — it is not what a ruler ought to love.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also said, "Yao used this to teach Danzhu — hardly fitting for a sovereign's pastime.

sentences.zh: 」雖數忤旨，而蒙賞賜，猶異餘人。

translations.literal: " Though he repeatedly went against the Emperor's intent, he still received rewards and was treated differently from others.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he often offended the throne, he still received rewards unlike anyone else.

sentences.zh: 遷兼中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，愿常侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took to his bed with illness, Yuan constantly attended with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill, Yuan constantly attended him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 帝素能食，尤好逐夷，以銀缽盛蜜漬之，一食數缽。

translations.literal: The Emperor had always been able to eat and especially loved zhuyi, storing it in a silver bowl steeped in honey — eating several bowls at one sitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always eaten heartily and especially loved pickled fish (zhuyi), kept in silver bowls steeped in honey — several bowls at a sitting.

sentences.zh: 謂揚州刺史王景文曰：「此是奇味，卿頗足不？

translations.literal: He said to Wang Jingwen, Governor of Yangzhou, "This is a marvelous flavor — do you have enough of it?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yangzhou Governor Wang Jingwen, "This is a rare delicacy — do you get enough of it?

sentences.zh: 」景文曰：「臣夙好此物，貧素致之甚難。

translations.literal: " Jingwen said, "Your servant has long loved this food; in poverty and plain living it is very hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingwen replied, "I have always loved it, but in poverty it is hard to come by.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 食逐夷積多，胷腹痞脹，氣將絕。

translations.literal: Eating zhuyi accumulated in quantity; his chest and belly became distended and blocked; his breath was nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Too much zhuyi distended his chest and belly until he could scarcely breathe.

sentences.zh: 左右啓飲數升酢酒，乃消。

translations.literal: Attendants reported that drinking several sheng of vinegar wine cleared it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants said several sheng of vinegar wine relieved it.

sentences.zh: 疾大困，一食汁滓猶至三升，水患積久，藥不復效。

translations.literal: The illness grew severe; a single meal of dregs and juice still reached three sheng; water illness had accumulated long, and medicine no longer had effect.
translations.idiomatic: The illness worsened; he still consumed three sheng of broth dregs per meal; chronic fluid retention defied medicine.

sentences.zh: 大漸日，正坐，呼道人，合掌便絕。

translations.literal: On the day of his final decline he sat upright, called a Daoist priest, joined his palms, and expired.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he sat upright, summoned a Daoist, joined his palms, and died.

sentences.zh: 愿以侍疾久，轉正員郎。

translations.literal: Yuan, for long attendance in illness, was transferred to regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For long attendance during the illness, Yuan was made a regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉平太守，在郡不治生產。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Jinping and in the commandery did not manage production for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Grand Administrator of Jinping, he undertook no profiteering in office.

sentences.zh: 前政與民交關，質錄其兒婦，愿遣人於道奪取將還。

translations.literal: The previous administration had dealings with the people and held their daughter-in-law as pledge; Yuan sent men on the road to seize her back and return her.
translations.idiomatic: The prior magistrate had seized a woman as pledge in a dispute; Yuan sent men to intercept her on the road and restore her.

sentences.zh: 在郡立學堂教授。

translations.literal: In the commandery he established a school for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he founded a school for instruction.

sentences.zh: 郡舊出髯蛇膽，可爲藥，有餉愿蛇者，愿不忍殺，放二十里外山中，一夜蛇還牀下。

translations.literal: The commandery traditionally produced bile from the bearded snake, usable as medicine. Someone presented Yuan with a snake; Yuan could not bear to kill it and released it twenty li into the mountains — in one night the snake returned beneath his bed.
translations.idiomatic: The region supplied bearded-snake bile for medicine. When someone gave Yuan a live snake, he released it twenty li into the hills; overnight it returned under his bed.

sentences.zh: 復送四十里外山，經宿，復還故處。

translations.literal: He sent it again forty li into the mountains; after one night it returned to the former place.
translations.idiomatic: He released it forty li farther; after a night it returned again.

sentences.zh: 愿更令遠，乃不復歸，論者以爲仁心所致也。

translations.literal: Yuan had it taken still farther, and it did not return; commentators held this was due to his humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had it taken still farther, and it did not return — which commentators attributed to his humane nature.

sentences.zh: 海邊有越王石，常隱雲霧。

translations.literal: By the sea there was a Yue King Stone, usually hidden in cloud and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Off the coast stood a Yue King Stone, usually shrouded in mist.

sentences.zh: 相傳云：「清廉太守乃得見。

translations.literal: Tradition said, "Only an incorrupt Grand Administrator can see it.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition said only an incorrupt magistrate could see it.

sentences.zh: 」愿往觀視，清徹無隱蔽。

translations.literal: " Yuan went to view it; it was clear and without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan went to look — the stone stood clear, unobscured.

sentences.zh: 後琅邪王秀之爲郡，與朝士書曰：「此郡承虞公之後，善政猶存，遺風易遵，差得無事。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Xiuzhi of Langya was in the commandery, he wrote to court gentlemen, "This commandery follows upon Lord Yu; good government still remains, the legacy easy to follow — one may get by without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Xiuzhi of Langye, taking the post, wrote to colleagues: "This commandery follows Lord Yu; good government endures and his legacy is easy to follow — affairs run fairly smoothly.

sentences.zh: 」以母老解職，除後軍將軍。

translations.literal: " He resigned because his mother was old and was appointed General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: " He resigned when his mother grew old and was appointed General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 褚淵常詣愿，不在，見其眠牀上積塵埃，有書數袠。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan often called on Yuan; when he was not in, he saw dust piled on the sleeping couch and several bundles of books.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan often visited Yuan; finding him out, he saw dust on the bed and several bundles of books.

sentences.zh: 淵歎曰：「虞君之清，一至於此。

translations.literal: Yuan sighed and said, "Lord Yu's purity extends even to this.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan sighed, "Lord Yu's austerity reaches even to this.

sentences.zh: 」令人掃地拂牀而去。

translations.literal: " He had someone sweep the floor and dust the bed, then left.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the floor swept and the bed dusted, then left.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Director of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 兄季，爲上虞令，卒。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji was magistrate of Shangyu and died.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji, magistrate of Shangyu, died.

sentences.zh: 愿從省步還家，不待詔便歸東。

translations.literal: Yuan returned home on foot from the Secretariat, and without awaiting an edict went back east.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan walked home from the Secretariat and, without awaiting imperial orders, returned east.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，遷廷尉，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and transferred to Minister of Justice, retaining his directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and Minister of Justice, retaining his Eastern Pavilion post.

sentences.zh: 愿嘗事宋明帝，齊初宋神主遷汝陰廟，愿拜辭流涕。

translations.literal: Yuan had once served Emperor Ming of Song; at the beginning of Qi, when the Song imperial tablets were moved to the Ruyin temple, Yuan bowed in farewell with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had served Emperor Ming of Song; when Qi began and Song's spirit tablets moved to the Ruyin temple, he bowed farewell in tears.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 愿著《五經論問》，撰《會稽記》，文翰數十篇。

translations.literal: Yuan authored Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and several tens of literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and several dozen essays.

sentences.zh: 劉懷慰字彥泰，平原平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaiwei, styled Yantai, was a native of Pingyuan in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaiwei, courtesy name Yantai, was from Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖奉伯，元嘉中，爲冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengbo, in the Yuanjia era, was Chief Clerk to the Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengbo served as Chief Clerk to the Champion General under Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 父乘民，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chengmin was Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengmin was Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 懷慰初爲桂陽王征北板行參軍。

translations.literal: Huaiwei was first a Traveling Clerk on the staff of the Prince of Guiyang's Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei began as Traveling Clerk on the Prince of Guiyang's northern campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 乘民死於義嘉事難，懷慰持喪，不食醯醬，冬月不絮衣。

translations.literal: Chengmin died in the Yijia troubles; Huaiwei observed mourning, ate no pickled sauces, and in winter months wore no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmin died in the Yijia upheaval; Huaiwei mourned without pickled food and wore no padded clothes even in winter.

sentences.zh: 養孤弟妹，事寡叔母，皆有恩義。

translations.literal: He raised his orphaned younger siblings and served his widowed aunt by marriage — all with kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He raised orphaned siblings and cared for a widowed aunt — all with devoted kindness.

sentences.zh: 復除邵陵王南中郎參軍，廣德令，尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Staff Officer of the Southern Central Army under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Southern Central Army staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.

sentences.zh: 懷慰宗從善明等，太祖心腹，懷慰亦豫焉。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's clansmen Shanming and others were the Founder Emperor's trusted inner circle; Huaiwei was also included among them.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen such as Shanming were the Founder's inner circle; Huaiwei was among them.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之有舊，令爲書戒喻攸之，太祖省之稱善。

translations.literal: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter admonishing Youzhi; the Founder Emperor read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Having old ties with Shen Youzhi, he was ordered to write admonishing him; the Founder read it and praised it.

sentences.zh: 除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，上欲置齊郡於京邑，議者以江右土沃，流民所歸，乃治瓜步，以懷慰爲輔國將軍、齊郡太守。

translations.literal: When the State of Qi was established, the sovereign wished to place Qi Commandery in the capital region. Discussants held that the lands south of the Yangtze were fertile and a destination for displaced people, so they instead administered Guabu, appointing Huaiwei General Who Assists the State and Grand Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded, the court wished to seat Qi Commandery in the capital district; debaters noted the fertile south attracted migrants, so they governed from Guabu instead, making Huaiwei General Who Assists the State and Grand Administrator of Qi.

sentences.zh: 上謂懷慰曰：「齊邦是王業所基，吾方以爲顯任。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Huaiwei, "The state of Qi is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I am now appointing you to a conspicuous post."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Huaiwei, "Qi is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I am giving you a post of real consequence."

sentences.zh: 經理之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: All matters of administration I entirely entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: All administrative matters I entrust entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 」又手勑曰：「有文事者，必有武備。

translations.literal: " He also wrote by hand: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be martial preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote in his own hand: "Civil affairs require martial preparedness.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿玉環刀一口。

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you one jade-ringed knife.
translations.idiomatic: I now grant you a jade-ringed knife.

sentences.zh: 」懷慰至郡，修治城郭，安集居民，墾廢田二百頃，決沈湖灌溉。

translations.literal: " When Huaiwei reached the commandery he repaired the walls, settled the residents, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened the Shen Lake for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: " At his post he repaired the walls, resettled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of fallow land, and opened the Shen Lake for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 不受禮謁，民有餉其新米一斛者，懷慰出所食麥飯示之，曰：「旦食有餘，幸不煩此。

translations.literal: He did not accept courtesy calls; when the people offered him one hu of new rice, Huaiwei brought out the wheat gruel he ate and showed them, saying, "My morning meal already suffices — kindly do not trouble yourselves with this.
translations.idiomatic: He refused gifts; when someone offered a hu of new rice, he showed his plain wheat meal and said, "Breakfast already fills me — please spare this trouble.

sentences.zh: 」因著《廉吏論》以達其意。

translations.literal: " He then composed On Incorrupt Officials to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote On Incorrupt Officials to make his intent plain.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，手勑褒賞。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor heard of it and wrote a hand-edict praising and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder heard and sent a handwritten edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 進督秦、沛二郡。

translations.literal: He was advanced to supervise Qin and Pei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervise Qin and Pei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 妻子在都，賜米三百斛。

translations.literal: His wife and children were in the capital; he was granted three hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: His family remained in the capital; he received three hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 兖州刺史柳世隆與懷慰書曰：「膠東淵化，潁川致美，以今方古，曾何足云。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, Inspector of Yanzhou, wrote to Huaiwei, "Jiaodong was civilized in the depths, Yingchuan achieved beauty — compared with antiquity, how can the present even be spoken of?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Liu Shilong wrote: "Jiaodong was transformed in the depths, Yingchuan achieved excellence — set against antiquity, the present scarcely bears mention.

sentences.zh: 」在郡二年，遷正員郎，領青冀二州中正。

translations.literal: " After two years in the commandery he was transferred to regular Attendant and concurrently head of the Qing and Ji selection offices.
translations.idiomatic: " After two years he became a regular Attendant and head of the Qing and Ji selection offices.

sentences.zh: 懷慰本名聞慰，世祖卽位，以與舅氏名同，勑改之。

translations.literal: Huaiwei original name was Wenwei; when the Shizu Emperor took the throne, because it matched his maternal uncle name, he was ordered to change it.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu took the throne, it matched his uncle name and he was ordered to change it.

sentences.zh: 出監東陽郡，爲吏民所安。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise Dongyang Commandery and brought peace to officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to supervise Dongyang, he won the trust of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 還兼安陸王北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: On return he concurrently served as Northern Central Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Northern Central Army staff officer to the Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming he died.

sentences.zh: 年四十五。

translations.literal: He was forty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-five.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，謂僕射徐孝嗣曰：「劉懷慰若在，朝廷不憂無清吏也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he said to Attendant-in-Chief Xu Xiaosi, "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would not worry about lacking incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, he told Xu Xiaosi, "Had Liu Huaiwei lived, the court would never lack honest officials.

sentences.zh: 」懷慰與濟陽江淹、陳郡袁彖善，亦著文翰。

translations.literal: " Huaiwei was friendly with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Can of Chen commandery, and also composed literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: " He was close to Jiang Yan and Yuan Can and also wrote essays.

sentences.zh: 永明初，獻《皇德論》云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he presented the Discourse on Imperial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming he presented the Discourse on Imperial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 裴昭明，河東聞喜人，宋太中大夫松之孫也。

translations.literal: Pei Zhaoming of Wenxi in Hedong was grandson of Song Grand Palace Grandee Pei Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhaoming of Wenxi, Hedong, was grandson of the Song historian Pei Songzhi.

sentences.zh: 父駰，南中郎參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yin was a Southern Central Army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin was a Southern Central Army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 昭明少傳儒史之業。

translations.literal: Zhaoming in youth transmitted the work of Confucian learning and history.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhaoming mastered Confucian and historical studies.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，爲太學博士。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he was a Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taishi he became an Imperial University erudite.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「太子婚，納徵用玉璧虎皮，未詳何所准據。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: "For the Crown Prince marriage, betrothal gifts use jade bi and tiger skin — it is not detailed on what authority this rests.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported: "The Crown Prince betrothal uses jade bi and tiger skin — on what authority?"

sentences.zh: 」昭明議：「禮納徵，儷皮爲庭實，鹿皮也。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming argued: "In ritual betrothal, paired skins are court offerings — deer skin.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming argued: "Ritual betrothal uses paired skins as court gifts — deer skin.

sentences.zh: 晉太子納妃注『以虎皮二』。

translations.literal: The Jin note on the Crown Prince taking a consort reads, with two tiger skins.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin commentary on the crown prince marriage reads two tiger skins.

sentences.zh: 太元中，公主納徵，虎豹皮各一。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, for a princess betrothal, one tiger skin and one leopard skin each.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan, a princess betrothal used one tiger and one leopard skin each.

sentences.zh: 豈其謂婚禮不詳。

translations.literal: Could this mean the marriage rites are not detailed?
translations.idiomatic: Surely this does not mean the marriage rites lack detail.

sentences.zh: 王公之差，故取虎豹文蔚以尊其事。

translations.literal: The difference for princes and dukes — therefore tiger and leopard patterns in splendor are taken to honor the affair.
translations.idiomatic: For princes and dukes, tiger and leopard pelts honor the occasion.

sentences.zh: 虎豹雖文，而徵禮所不言，熊羆雖古，而婚禮所不及，珪璋雖美，或爲用各異。

translations.literal: Though tiger and leopard have pattern, betrothal rites do not mention them; though bear and brown bear are ancient, wedding rites do not reach them; though jade tablets are beautiful, usages may differ.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger and leopard appear in splendor but not in betrothal canon; bear appears in antiquity but not in wedding rites; jade is beautiful but usages differ.

sentences.zh: 今宜准的經誥，凡諸僻謬，一皆詳正。

translations.literal: Now one should take the classics as standard; wherever there are irregularities, all should be examined and corrected in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Standards should follow the classics; every irregularity should be corrected.

sentences.zh: 」於是有司參議，加珪璋，豹熊羆皮各二。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the relevant office deliberated and added jade tablets, with two leopard skins and two bear-and-brown-bear skins each.
translations.idiomatic: " The office then added jade tablets and two leopard and two bear skins each.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，出爲長沙郡丞，罷任，刺史王蘊謂之曰：「卿清貧，必無還資。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he went out as Assistant Administrator of Changsha Commandery. When his term ended, Inspector Wang Yun said to him, "You are poor and pure — you surely have no returning wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was Changsha assistant administrator; on leaving, Inspector Wang Yun said, "You are so poor you will have nothing to bring back.

sentences.zh: 湘中人士有須一禮之命者，我不愛也。

translations.literal: If gentlemen of Xiang need a single gift of courtesy, I do not begrudge it.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone in Xiang needs a parting gift, I will not begrudge it.

sentences.zh: 」昭明曰：「下官忝爲邦佐，不能光益上府，豈以鴻都之事仰累清風。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming said, "Your subordinate is humbly a commandery aide and cannot brighten the superior prefecture — how could I burden your pure reputation with Hongdu affairs?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming replied, "As your aide I cannot enhance the prefecture — I could not burden your integrity with such errands.

sentences.zh: 」歷祠部通直郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Director of Rites and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Rites and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，使虜，世祖謂之曰：「以卿有將命之才，使還，當以一郡相賞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was sent on a mission to the barbarians; the Shizu Emperor said to him, "Because you have the talent to bear imperial orders, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 3 he went north; Emperor Wu said, "You have talent for embassies — on your return I will reward you with a commandery.

sentences.zh: 」還爲始安內史。

translations.literal: On return he became Internal Governor of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Internal Governor of Shian.

sentences.zh: 郡民龔玄宣，云神人與其玉印玉板書，不須筆，吹紙便成字。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Gong Xuanyuan, said a spirit-man gave him jade seals and jade boards with writing — no brush needed; blowing on paper characters appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xuanyuan claimed a spirit gave him jade seals and boards: blow on paper and characters formed without a brush.

sentences.zh: 自稱「龔聖人」，以此惑衆。

translations.literal: He called himself the Sage Gong and used this to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Sage Gong and misled the crowd.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守敬事之，昭明付獄治罪。

translations.literal: Former commandery chiefs had honored him; Zhaoming put him in prison and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Prior magistrates had honored him; Zhaoming imprisoned and punished him.

sentences.zh: 及還，甚貧罄。

translations.literal: When he returned he was utterly destitute.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was utterly destitute.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「裴昭明罷郡還，遂無宅。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor said, "Pei Zhaoming finished his commandery and has no dwelling at all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said, "Pei Zhaoming left his post with no home to his name.

sentences.zh: 我不諳書，不知古人中誰比？

translations.literal: I am not versed in books — which man of antiquity does he resemble?
translations.idiomatic: I am no reader — which ancient official does he resemble?

sentences.zh: 」遷射聲校尉。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Commandant of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣北使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again sent on a northern mission.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he was sent north again.

sentences.zh: 建武初，爲王玄邈安北長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was Chief Clerk to Wang Xuanyao Pacification of the North army and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu he was chief clerk to Wang Xuanyao and Grand Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 明帝以其在事無所啓奏，代還，責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because in office he made no memorials or reports, replaced and recalled him and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming recalled him for filing no memorials and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 昭明曰：「臣不欲競執關楗故耳。

translations.literal: Zhaoming said, "Your servant did not wish to compete over bolts and bars — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "I did not wish to wrangle over gate bolts — that is all.

sentences.zh: 」昭明歷郡皆有勤績，常謂人曰：「人生何事須聚蓄，一身之外，亦復何須？

translations.literal: " Zhaoming in every commandery had diligent achievement; he often told people, "What need has human life for amassing? Beyond one own person, what more is needed?
translations.idiomatic: " In every post he achieved much; he often said, "Why hoard in life? Beyond oneself, what is needed?

sentences.zh: 子孫若不才，我聚彼散；

translations.literal: If sons and grandsons lack talent, I gather and they scatter;
translations.idiomatic: If heirs lack talent, I gather and they squander;

sentences.zh: 若能自立，則不如一經。

translations.literal: if they can stand on their own, then one classic is better.
translations.idiomatic: if they can stand alone, one classic suffices.

sentences.zh: 」故終身不治產業。

translations.literal: " Therefore all his life he did not manage estates.
translations.idiomatic: " So he never built an estate.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟顗，字彥齊。

translations.literal: His cousin Yan, styled Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yan, courtesy name Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 少有異操。

translations.literal: In youth he had an unusual integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed unusual integrity.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，於總明觀聽講，不讓劉秉席，秉用爲參軍。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era, at the Zongming Observatory listening to lectures, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing; Bing employed him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At Taishi, in lectures at the Zongming Observatory, he would not yield seat to Liu Bing, who then took him on staff.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，爲奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengming era he was a Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shengming he was a Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，世子裴妃須外戚譜，顗不與，遂分籍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, the Heir Apparent Pei consort needed a maternal kin genealogy; Yan would not provide it and they split registers.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded, the heir Pei consort needed a kin genealogy; Yan refused and they split registers.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，上表誹謗，掛冠去，伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Yan submitted a memorial of slander, hung up his cap and left, and was executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: At the Founder accession Yan submitted a slanderous memorial, resigned, and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 沈憲字彥璋，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Xian, styled Yanzhang, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xian, courtesy name Yanzhang, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖說道，巴西梓潼二郡太守，父璞之，北中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuodao was Grand Administrator of Ba and Zitong in two commanderies; his father Puzhi was a Northern Central Army traveling staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Shuodao governed Ba and Zitong; father Puzhi was a Northern Central Army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 憲初應州辟，爲主簿。

translations.literal: Xian at first responded to a provincial summons and became chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service via provincial summons as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 少有幹局，歷臨首、餘杭令，巴陵王府佐，帶襄令，除駕部郎。

translations.literal: In youth he had administrative capacity; he served as magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, staff officer in the Prince of Baling household, concurrently magistrate of Xiang, and was appointed Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he showed administrative talent; he was magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, staff to the Prince of Baling, magistrate of Xiang, then Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝與憲棋，謂憲曰：「卿，廣州刺史才也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song played weiqi with Xian and said to Xian, "You have the talent of an Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming played weiqi with him and said, "You have the makings of a Guangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 」補烏程令，甚著政績。

translations.literal: " He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and achieved very manifest administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: " Appointed magistrate of Wucheng, he won striking renown.

sentences.zh: 太守褚淵歎之曰：「此人方員可施。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Chu Yuan sighed and said, "This man is square and round — deployable everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan sighed, "This man adapts to square or round — fit for any post.

sentences.zh: 」除通直郎，都水使者。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Regular Attendant and Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: " He became Regular Attendant and Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 長於吏事，居官有績。

translations.literal: Skilled in administrative affairs, in office he had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in administration, he performed well in every post.

sentences.zh: 除正員郎，補吳令，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed regular Attendant, supplemented as magistrate of Wu, and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became regular Attendant, magistrate of Wu, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，西中郎將晃爲豫州，太祖擢憲爲晃長史，南梁太守，行州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, Western Central Army General Huang was in Yuzhou; the Founder promoted Xian as Huang Chief Clerk, Grand Administrator of Nanliang, exercising provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year 2, when Huang held Yuzhou, the Founder made Xian his chief clerk and Nanliang administrator, acting for the province.

sentences.zh: 遷豫章王諮議，未拜，坐事免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Consultant to the Prince of Yuzhang but did not accept appointment; he sat in an affair and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred as consultant to the Prince of Yuzhang, he was dismissed before taking office over an affair.

sentences.zh: 復除安成王冠軍、武陵王征虜參軍，遷少府卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Champion staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng and Pacification staff officer to the Prince of Wuling, and transferred to Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed staff to the Princes of Ancheng and Wuling, then Minister of the Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 少府管掌市易，與民交關，有吏能者，皆更此職。

translations.literal: The Palace Supplies oversaw market trade and dealings with the people; those with administrative ability were all rotated through this post.
translations.idiomatic: That ministry managed markets and dealt with the public — a training post for able administrators.

sentences.zh: 遷王儉鎮軍長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk under Wang Jian Pacification army.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk to Wang Jian Pacification army.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄爲會稽，以憲爲左軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was in Kuaiji, Xian was made Left Army Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ye of Wuling held Kuaiji, Xian was his Left Army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 太祖以山陰戶衆難治，欲分爲兩縣。

translations.literal: The Founder, because Shanyin had a numerous population and was hard to govern, wished to divide it into two counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder wished to split overcrowded Shanyin into two counties.

sentences.zh: 世祖啓曰：「縣豈不可治，但用不得其人耳。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor memorialized, "A county surely can be governed — only the wrong man is used.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied, "A county can be governed — you merely need the right man.

sentences.zh: 」乃以憲帶山陰令，政聲大著。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xian was made concurrent magistrate of Shanyin, and his administrative fame was greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was made concurrent Shanyin magistrate with great renown.

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪請假東歸，謂人曰：「沈令料事特有天才。

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui requested leave to return east and said to people, "Magistrate Shen handling of affairs has a special genius for it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui, leaving for the east, said, "Magistrate Shen has a rare genius for affairs.

sentences.zh: 」加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: " He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 王敬則爲會稽，憲仍留爲鎮軍長史，令如故。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze was in Kuaiji; Xian remained as Pacification Army Chief Clerk with his orders unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze took Kuaiji, Xian stayed on as chief clerk with unchanged duties.

sentences.zh: 遷爲冠軍長史，行南豫州事，晉安王後軍長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Champion Chief Clerk, acting for Southern Yuzhou, then Rear Army Chief Clerk to the Prince of Jinan and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He became Champion chief clerk acting for Southern Yuzhou, then rear-army chief clerk to the Prince of Jinan and Guangling administrator.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明代爲南兖州，憲仍留爲冠軍長史，太守如故，頻行州府事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiyang Ziming replaced him in Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained Champion Chief Clerk with the same grand administership, frequently exercising provincial and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ziming of Xiyang took Southern Yanzhou, Xian stayed as chief clerk and administrator, often acting for province and prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，子明典籤劉道濟取府州五十人役自給，又役子明左右，及船仗贓私百萬，爲有司所奏，世祖怒，賜道濟死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming registrar Liu Daoji took fifty men from the prefecture and province for his own service, also used Ziming attendants, and embezzled a million in boats and gear — reported by the authorities; the Shizu Emperor was angry and ordered Daoji executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 8, registrar Liu Daoji impressed fifty officials for private use, embezzled a million in shipping — the Emperor ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 憲坐不糾，免官。

translations.literal: Xian sat because he did not investigate and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was dismissed for failing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 尋復爲長史、輔國將軍，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Soon he was again Chief Clerk and General Who Assists the State, then left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reappointed chief clerk and General Who Assists the State, he resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept appointment before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, he died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 當世稱爲良吏。

translations.literal: His age called him a good official.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries hailed him as a model magistrate.

sentences.zh: 憲同郡丘仲起，先是爲晉平郡，清廉自立。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongqi of Xian same commandery had earlier been Grand Administrator of Jinping, upright and self-reliant in purity.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongqi of the same commandery had governed Jinping with austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 褚淵歎曰：「見可欲心能不亂，此楊公所以遺子孫也。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan sighed and said, "To see what is desirable yet keep the heart unperturbed — this is why Duke Yang left counsel to his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan said, "To see temptation yet remain unmoved — that is why Duke Yang left his precepts to posterity.

sentences.zh: 」仲起字子震，少爲憲從伯領軍寅之所知。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi, styled Zizhen, in youth was known to Yin, Xian cousin and Pacification Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, was known in youth to Commander Yin, Xian cousin.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽中，爲太子領軍長史，官至廷尉。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era of Song he was Chief Clerk to the Crown Prince Pacification Army and reached Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Yuanhui he was crown-prince chief clerk and rose to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 李珪之字孔璋，江夏鍾武人也。

translations.literal: Li Guizhi, styled Kongzhang, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guizhi, courtesy name Kongzhang, was from Zhongwu in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 父祖皆爲縣令。

translations.literal: Father and grandfather were all county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Father and grandfather had both been county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 珪之少辟州從事。

translations.literal: Guizhi in youth was summoned as provincial staff.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guizhi entered provincial service.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，蔡興宗爲郢州，以珪之爲安西府佐，委以職事，清治見知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Taishi, Cai Xingzong was in Yingzhou and made Guizhi a staff officer of the Pacification of the West headquarters, entrusting him with duties; his clear governance won recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi, Cai Xingzong at Yingzhou took him on staff and entrusted affairs to him; his clarity won notice.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮西中郎諮議，右軍將軍，兼都水使者。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Consultant of the Western Central Army, General of the Right Army, and concurrently Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He became Western Central Army consultant, General of the Right Army, and Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 珪之歷職稱爲清能，除游擊將軍，兼使者如故。

translations.literal: Guizhi in successive posts was called clear and capable; he was appointed General of Guerrilla Warfare, concurrently Commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts Guizhi was known for clarity and competence; he was made General of Guerrilla Warfare while retaining his commissioner post.

sentences.zh: 轉兼少府，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，四年，滎陽毛惠素爲少府卿，吏才強而治事清刻。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang was Minister of the Palace Supplies — strong in administrative talent yet severe and clear in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in year four, Xingyang Mao Huisu served as Minister of the Palace Supplies — administratively forceful and rigorously impartial.

sentences.zh: 勑市銅官碧青一千二百斤供御畫，用錢六十萬。

translations.literal: He was ordered that the market copper office supply twelve hundred jin of malachite blue-green for imperial painting, using six hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the copper market office to supply twelve hundred jin of malachite pigment for imperial painting at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 有讒惠素納利者，世祖怒，勑尚書評賈，貴二十八萬餘，有司奏之，伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Huisu for taking profit; the Shizu Emperor was angry and ordered the Imperial Secretariat to assess the price, valuing it at more than two hundred eighty thousand; the relevant office memorialized and he was executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He was slandered for profiteering; Emperor Wu ordered a price review at over two hundred eighty thousand; the authorities memorialized and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 死後家徒四壁，上甚悔恨。

translations.literal: After death his house had only four bare walls; the sovereign deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his home was bare to the walls; the Emperor deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 孔琇之，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuzhi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuzhi was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖季恭，光祿大夫，父靈運，著作郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jigong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his father Lingyun was Composition Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Jigong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; father Lingyun was Composition Officer.

sentences.zh: 琇之初爲國子生，舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi at first was a student of the Imperial University and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi first studied at the Imperial University and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 除衞軍行參軍，員外郎，尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Traveling Staff Officer of the Guard Army, Attendant Outside the Office, and Director of the Three Dukes Office in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was Traveling Staff Officer of the Guard Army, Attendant Outside the Office, and Director of the Three Dukes Office.

sentences.zh: 出爲烏程令，有吏能。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wucheng and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as magistrate of Wucheng, he showed administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 還遷通直郎，補吳令。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to Regular Attendant and supplemented as magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became Regular Attendant and supplemented as magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 有小兒年十歲，偷刈隣家稻一束，琇之付獄治罪，或諫之，琇之曰：「十歲便能爲盜，長大何所不爲？

translations.literal: A small boy ten years old stole one sheaf of a neighbor rice; Xiuzhi put him in prison to punish the crime. Some admonished him; Xiuzhi said, "At ten he can already steal — grown, what will he not do?
translations.idiomatic: A ten-year-old stole a sheaf of a neighbor rice; Xiuzhi jailed him. When advised against it he said, "At ten he steals — grown, what will he not do?

sentences.zh: 」縣中皆震肅。

translations.literal: " Within the county all were awed and shaken into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: " The county was awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，又以職事知名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again became famous for professional achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, he won renown for his work.

sentences.zh: 轉前軍將軍，兼少府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Forward Army General and concurrently Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He became Forward Army General and concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，少府如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, retaining the Ministry of the Palace Supplies as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Valiant Cavalry while retaining the ministry post.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、高宗冠軍征虜長史、江夏內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk to the Pacification Army of the Crown Prince of Gaozong, and Internal Governor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk to the crown prince pacification army, and Internal Governor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 還爲正員常侍，兼左民尚書、廷尉卿。

translations.literal: On return he became regular Attendant of Constant Service, concurrently Director of the Ministry of the People on the Left and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was regular Attendant of Constant Service, concurrently Director of the Left Ministry of the People and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨海太守，在任清約，罷郡還，獻乾薑二十斤，世祖嫌少，及知琇之清，乃歎息。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Linhai; in office he was pure and abstemious. When his commandery term ended and he returned, he presented twenty jin of dried ginger; the Shizu Emperor thought it too little, but on learning Xiuzhi purity he sighed.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Administrator of Linhai he lived plainly; on leaving he offered twenty jin of dried ginger. Emperor Wu thought it meager, then sighed on learning his austerity.

sentences.zh: 除武陵王前軍長史，未拜，仍出爲輔國將軍，監吳興郡，尋拜太守，治稱清嚴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk to the Forward Army of the Prince of Wuling but did not accept appointment; he then went out as General Who Assists the State, supervising Wuxing Commandery, soon appointed Grand Administrator — his governance was called pure and strict.
translations.idiomatic: Made chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling, he declined; then supervised Wuxing and soon became Grand Administrator — governance famed as pure and strict.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：琴瑟不調，必解而更張也。

translations.literal: The historian says: When zither and lute are out of tune, one must untie and restring them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When lute and zither are out of tune, they must be restrung.

sentences.zh: 魏晉爲吏，稍與漢乖，苛猛之風雖衰，而仁愛之情亦減。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin in governing the people gradually diverged from Han ways; though the harsh and fierce wind declined somewhat, humane care also diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, governance gradually diverged from Han ways: harshness faded, but humane care diminished too.

sentences.zh: 局以峻法，限以常條，以必世之仁未及宣理，而朞月之望已求治術。

translations.literal: Confined by severe laws and limited by routine statutes, the benevolence of an enduring age had not yet reached full dissemination of principle, yet the hope of a single month already sought techniques of order.
translations.idiomatic: Bound by harsh laws and routine statutes, enduring benevolence had not yet spread, yet a month horizon already demanded results.

sentences.zh: 先公後私，在己未易，割民奉國，於物非難，期之救過，所利苟免。

translations.literal: Public affairs before private — hard for oneself; cutting the people to serve the state — not difficult for things; what is sought is rescue from fault, the benefit is mere escape.
translations.idiomatic: Putting the public before the private is hard on oneself; taxing the people for the state is easier — what is sought is escape from blame.

sentences.zh: 且目見可欲，嗜好方流，貪以敗官，取與違義，吏之不臧，罔非由此。

translations.literal: Moreover the eye sees what is desirable and preferences flow forth; greed ruins office, taking and giving violate righteousness — the corruption of officials has no source outside this.
translations.idiomatic: What the eye desires becomes habit; greed ruins office and violates righteousness — official corruption stems from nothing else.

sentences.zh: 擿姦辯偽，誠俟異識，垂名著績，唯有廉平。

translations.literal: Exposing wickedness and distinguishing falsity truly awaits a different insight; to leave a lasting mark in achievement, only incorruption and fairness suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing fraud awaits special insight; lasting achievement rests only on incorruption and fairness.

sentences.zh: 今世之治民，未有出於此也。

translations.literal: Governing the people in the present age has not gone beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the people today has not surpassed this principle.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蒸蒸小民，吏職長親。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The teeming common people — officials and duties are their long kin.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The teeming masses — officials are their enduring kin.

sentences.zh: 棼亂須理，卹隱歸仁。

translations.literal: When disorder must be set right, comfort and pity return to humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder must be ordered, succor returns to humaneness.

sentences.zh: 枉直交瞀，寬猛代陳。

translations.literal: Wrong and right cross in confusion; lenience and severity alternate in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong tangle; lenience and severity alternate.

sentences.zh: 伊何導物，貴在清身。

translations.literal: What guides the multitude? The precious thing is a pure body.
translations.idiomatic: What guides the people? A clean personal example.

translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.

translations.idiomatic: The full text is collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
